videos.title: Who Is Satoshi Nakamoto? The $90 Billion Mystery #shorts
videos.description:
On October 31, 2008, someone called Satoshi Nakamoto published the Bitcoin white paper. The first block contained a newspaper headline about bank bailouts. In 2011 Satoshi wrote he had "moved on to other things" and disappeared. An estimated 1.1 million bitcoin linked to Satoshi have never moved.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satoshi_Nakamoto

#shorts #bitcoin #satoshi #crypto #mystery

videos.title: The $800 Million Pizza 🍕 #shorts
videos.description:
On May 22, 2010, programmer Laszlo Hanyecz paid 10,000 bitcoin for two pizzas – worth about $41 back then. At around $82,000 per bitcoin (October 2026), those coins would be worth over $800 million. That's why May 22 is Bitcoin Pizza Day.

Source: https://www.coindesk.com/learn/what-is-bitcoin-pizza-day/
⚠️ Not financial advice.

#shorts #bitcoin #crypto #pizza #history

videos.title: Why There Will Never Be More Than 21 Million Bitcoin #shorts
videos.description:
Every ~10 minutes a new block is added to the chain. Miners race to guess a special number, and the winner gets new bitcoin – currently 3.125 BTC per block. About every four years that reward is cut in half, so the last bitcoin is expected around the year 2140.

⚠️ Not financial advice.

#shorts #bitcoin #crypto #halving #mining

videos.title: Crypto Explained in 45 Seconds #shorts
videos.description:
What is cryptocurrency? Instead of a bank keeping the list of who owns what, the list – the blockchain – is shared and copied on thousands of computers. Bitcoin, Ethereum, stablecoins and Dogecoin explained in seconds.

videos.title: This Steak Was 3D Printed 🥩 #shorts
videos.description:
Redefine Meat 3D prints plant-based steaks layer by layer, with a "muscle" and a "fat" part to copy the texture of real meat – made from soy and pea protein, chickpeas, beets and coconut fat. It has been served in restaurants in cities like London, Berlin and Amsterdam. Would you try it?

Source: https://www.techbrew.com/stories/2021/11/17/3d-printed-steaks-are-now-being-served-at-restaurants-acro

videos.title: Z Anti-Aliasing: The Free Slicer Setting That Removes Layer Lines
videos.description: Every 3D printer prints flat layers – that's why curved and sloped surfaces look like a staircase. Z anti-aliasing (ZAA) is an open-source trick where the nozzle moves up and down inside a single layer and follows the real surface. No new hardware, just one setting. In this video: why the staircase happens, how ZAA works, real test results, the open-source story behind it, how to try it in OrcaSli

videos.title: Strangers 3D Print Hands for Kids – For Free ❤️ #shorts
videos.description:
e-NABLE is a global network of volunteers who 3D print prosthetic hands for kids and adults, for free. Many designs are powered by the wrist, and the materials for one hand can cost around $35 – so when kids grow, a new one is simply printed bigger.

Source: https://enablingthefuture.org/learn/faq/

#shorts #3dprinting #enable #prosthetics #wholesome

videos.title: Why Everyone 3D Prints This Little Boat #shorts
videos.description:
Meet 3DBenchy, the "jolly 3D printing torture test" from 2015. The hull, the roof, the arched doors and the tiny name on the back each test something different. It's believed to be the most printed 3D model in the world – and since 2025 it's in the public domain.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3DBenchy

#shorts #3dprinting #benchy #3dbenchy #3dprinter

videos.title: Is 3D Printing Safe? Fumes, Resin & Fire Risks Explained
videos.description:
A nozzle at over 200 °C, plastic fumes, liquid chemicals, and a machine that runs for hours. So is 3D printing actually safe? Short answer: yes, if you know the risks. This video covers the four big ones (air quality, resin, fire and burns) and ends with a simple safety checklist.

videos.title: NASA Emailed a Wrench to Space 🚀 #shorts
videos.description:
In December 2014, Commander Barry Wilmore needed a ratchet wrench on the International Space Station. Instead of waiting months for a rocket, engineers sent the design file up to the 3D printer on board – and about four hours later he had a brand new wrench.

Source: https://www.csoonline.com/article/2861865/iss-3d-printed-ratchet-after-nasa-emailed-the-wrench-to-space.html

#shorts #nasa #space #

videos.title: This Dragon Came Out of a 3D Printer Already Moving 🐉 #shorts
videos.description:
No glue, no assembly: print-in-place models come off the printer in one piece, with every joint already free. The trick is a tiny gap of less than half a millimeter between the parts. Hinges, chains, even gears – all printed in one go.

#shorts #3dprinting #printinplace #articulateddragon #3dprinted

videos.title: Arduino vs ESP32 vs Raspberry Pi Pico: Which Should You Buy First?
videos.description:
Arduino Uno, ESP32 or Raspberry Pi Pico 2 – which microcontroller should you buy first? In this video I compare all three side by side: specs, the 5 V vs 3.3 V gotcha, programming (Arduino IDE, MicroPython, ESP-IDF, Pico SDK), wireless and price. At the end you get a clear recommendation, plus my personal pick.
